design:
Part of the phase 2 dogfooding programme (epic: bn op-igib).

## The abstraction

Doubly heterogeneous media should become a **first-class concept**, with a
clean separation between what the material *is* and how it is *tracked*:

```
Material          composition / nuclear state
   |
Medium            spatial material structure
   |
Region / Geometry
   |
Transport representation
```

**Do not conflate physical material definitions with tracking algorithms.**

For an HTR:

```
HTR core
  |
  +-- pebble-bed heterogeneity
  |      helium + pebbles
  |
  +-- pebble
         graphite + dispersed TRISO particles
```

Two requirements follow, and they are the whole point:

1. **The physical heterogeneous model is defined once.**
2. **Different MC representations are selectable independently**, against that
   same model.

If changing from explicit CSG to delta tracking requires rebuilding the
material description, the abstraction has failed.

## Deliverable: a design note

A short design note describing the intended heterogeneous-medium abstraction
and the roles of explicit surface tracking, delta tracking and CLS. This is a
listed deliverable of the programme, not optional documentation — the tracking
hierarchy issue depends on it being written down.

## Dogfood task

Give a fresh Haiku agent a public-API task centred on the HTR direction, built
on this abstraction. Realistic engineering framing, not a transcription of an
existing example.

## Prior art to check before designing

`outram-mc-libs` already carries relevant pieces — `stochastic::{cls, scls,
medium, spatial_index}`, `pebble_beds::{delta_tracking, keff_delta,
sphere_packing, crp_packing}`, and TRISO helpers. Phase 1's repeated lesson was
**"data model exists, access seam missing"**: check what is already implemented
before adding types, and prefer exposing existing orchestration seams over
introducing parallel ones.
title: Heterogeneous-medium abstraction: Material / Medium / Region / Transport, plus design note

description:
Two related errors, same root cause — the rand/getrandom stack refuses to build for wasm32-unknown-unknown without being told where entropy comes from, because the bare wasm32-unknown-unknown target has no OS:

  kovan, outram-park-digital-twin-engine:
    'to use uuid on wasm32-unknown-unknown, specify a source of randomness using one of the js/rng feature flags'
  tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver:
    'The wasm32-unknown-unknown targets are not supported by default; you may need to enable the js feature'

Fix is a target-gated feature, e.g. for getrandom 0.2 the 'js' feature, or for 0.3 the wasm_js backend plus the matching RUSTFLAGS cfg. CHECK WHICH MAJOR VERSION the tree actually resolves before choosing — getrandom changed this mechanism between 0.2 and 0.3 and the wrong advice is a common time sink.

Add only under [target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies] so native and Android builds are untouched.

Question worth answering rather than assuming: does the crate actually NEED randomness on wasm, or is uuid/rand pulled in by something that could itself be feature-gated off? Cutting the dependency is better than satisfying it. tampines and tuas in particular should be checked — a thermal-hydraulics solver wanting entropy at all is worth a second look.

Acceptance: all four pass the wasm --lib check; native and Android unchanged.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Done. tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver and outram-park-digital-twin-engine all pass the wasm --lib check.

Two DIFFERENT getrandom majors were in play, needing different mechanisms — the bead warned about exactly this and it was worth checking rather than assuming:

  getrandom 0.3 (tampines, tuas, via peroxide -> rand):
    Needs BOTH the 'wasm_js' feature AND --cfg getrandom_backend="wasm_js".
    The feature alone is insufficient and getrandom errors saying so. The cfg
    now lives in a new .cargo/config.toml scoped to [target.wasm32-unknown-unknown],
    so a plain 'cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown' works with no extra
    environment — which is what the gate runs.

  getrandom 0.2 + uuid (digital-twin-engine, via async-opcua):
    NOT satisfied. CUT instead, which is what this bead said to prefer.

On the bead's own question — 'does the crate actually NEED randomness, or is it pulled in by something that could be gated off?':

  tampines/tuas: it comes from peroxide, which depends on rand UNCONDITIONALLY with no feature to disable it. Cutting would mean replacing peroxide's CubicSpline across ~39 sites in tuas — its own job, not this one. So satisfying it was the smaller correct change here, and the reasoning is recorded in .cargo/config.toml rather than left as a mystery flag.

  digital-twin-engine: it came from async-opcua, which a browser cannot use at all. Target-gating the whole OPC-UA/mDNS/filesystem stack off wasm (async-opcua, tokio, mdns-sd, directories, local-ip-address, env_logger) removed getrandom 0.2 AND uuid outright, and took the crate from 57 errors to 0. The ciet_opcua / opcua_core / htgr_opcua modules are gated to match.

That last one also DELIVERS op-eeqw.2 (GH #39 Phase 1), which asked for exactly this gating for the htgr browser demo. Two epics, one change.

All gates are wasm-only: async-opcua was verified Android-clean on 2026-07-28 and stays ungated there.

Verification: all three pass wasm --lib; all three pass native --lib and aarch64-linux-android --lib with 0 errors; cargo check --workspace --lib native has 0 errors.

title: wasm class C: getrandom/uuid wasm randomness backend (4 crates)

description:
Filed 2026-08-12 on completing the TwoFluid1d solver core (op-62vf), as a hand-off to whoever writes the six-equation benchmark cases (op-s1a0).

WHAT THE SOLVER OFFERS. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs:
  TwoFluid1d::new(pipe, exchange, pressure, temperature, dt) -> Result<Self>
  TwoFluid1d::bubbly(pipe, pressure, temperature, dt)  -- Schiller-Naumann + Ranz-Marshall + spherical, 1 mm
  set_temperature_profile(&[ThermodynamicTemperature])  -- for the Hendrie non-isothermal profile
  set_left_boundary / set_right_boundary (TwoFluidBoundary::{Closed, PrescribedVelocity, ChokedOutlet})
  set_virtual_mass_coefficient / set_initial_void_fraction / set_residual_alpha / set_outer_correctors / set_pressure_under_relaxation
  step() -> Result<TwoFluidReport>
  read-only: pressure, void_fraction, liquid_fraction, vapour_/liquid_density, vapour_/liquid_enthalpy, vapour_/liquid_temperature, saturation_temperature, vapour_/liquid_face_velocity, slip_velocity, mixture_density, inventory, total_enthalpy, outlet_mass_flow

TwoFluidReport carries time, outlet_mass_flow, max/min_void_fraction, max_thermal_nonequilibrium, max_slip, inventory, max_courant, max_volume_residual, outer_correctors_used, outlet_choked, mass_transfer_limited_cells, residual_alpha_floor_events.

READ THESE BEFORE STARTING, both filed 2026-08-12:
1. 'low-void starts refuse -- vapour cannot shed its expansion work'. Edwards-O'Brien starts 57 K SUBCOOLED, which is exactly the regime that refuses after 10-15 steps. A two-fluid Edwards case is BLOCKED on that, not merely unwritten. Do not work around it by tuning the initial void fraction until it runs -- that is choosing a model parameter to get a benchmark to pass.
2. 'no Dirichlet-pressure boundary'. There is no ReservoirInlet or PressureOutlet, so a Marviken-style vessel discharge has no inlet boundary to use.

WHAT IS OBLIGATORY IF A CASE IS WRITTEN, per crates/tampines/docs/six-equation-regularisation.md section 9.5:
  - a grid-refinement study, with the observed order -- the system is NOT known to be well posed, so refinement may not improve the answer, and reporting a single-mesh number would be misleading;
  - a sensitivity of the headline result to C_vm over at least [0, 0.5]. two_fluid_tests::the_answer_moves_with_c_vm_and_the_sensitivity_is_reported shows how, and measured on the demonstrator case: 8.4 % spread in max |T_g - T_l|, 1.1 % in slip, 0.16 % in outlet mass flow;
  - the same for the initial void fraction, which is a model parameter with no measured provenance.

A WORKING STARTING POINT EXISTS: two_fluid_tests::a_two_phase_blowdown_marches_without_refusing runs the Edwards geometry from a SATURATED two-phase state and completes -- 667 steps at 8 cells, and 10002 steps (full 300 ms) at 24 cells, reaching 19.3 K of thermal non-equilibrium and 1.46 m/s of slip. That is not Edwards (wrong initial condition) but it is the harness shape a case would reuse.
title: tampines: Edwards-O'Brien and Marviken two-fluid (6-eqn) cases -- API is ready, read the two blocker beads first
